To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular position of the acoustic scale within a redshift bin is sensitive to the angular diameter of the bin, and the redshift dispersion of the galaxies within the bin.
the position of the baryon oscillations in the angular correlation function is shifted by projection effects, and that these effects are not well described by the standard Limber approximation.

the angular diameter distance can be measured to 1 % accuracy from the position of the baryonic acoustic peak in the angular correlation function of galaxies, provided a redshift bin of width 0.1 can be constructed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of projection on the baryon oscillations, which are of interest to the photometric redshifting community.
the effect of redshift binning on angular clustering of photometrically selected galaxies, and we find that the Limber approximation is only valid when the binning is sufficiently thin.
the effects of projection, redshift binning, and photometric redshift errors on the baryon oscillation signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

photometric redshifts must be measured to an accuracy of Δ σz ≲ 10 -3 in order to recover the acoustic peak, which, at z ≃ 0.5, translates into Δz ≲ 0.02, which is comparable to the expected redshift uncertainty of the next generation of photometric redshift experiments.

the baryon peak can be detected in the angular clustering of galaxies with photometric redshifts, but the precision of the measurement will depend on the accuracy of the redshift determination, which will be a major challenge.

, in the absence of a significant improvement on the current understanding of the physics of the interstellar and intergalactic media, and of the physics of galaxy formation, the baryon peak is a robust, but challenging, probe of the expansion history of the universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a redshift bin width of Δz = 0.05 is the optimal value, with a photometric redshift accuracy of σz = 0. 01, for a redshift range of 0.2 ≤ z ≤ 0.8.

the angular baryon acoustic oscillation peak in the angular correlation function can be used to measure the angular diameter distance with a precision of 1 % in the near future, provided the total redshift error can be determined to within 1 %.
the angular diameter distance and the Hubble constant can be determined to a few percent, while the equation of state of the dark energy can only be measured at the level of a few percent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular diameter distance is the quantity that is most directly constrained by the position of the acoustic feature, and the redshift binning scheme must therefore be optimized accordingly.
the photometric redshifting of future surveys must be performed with great precision if they are to be used to constrain the dark energy equation-of-state parameter.
the baryon oscillations in the galaxy correlation function will be observable, and will provide a powerful probe of dark energy.
